paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. Jesus is heavy-hearted and trying to get alone, and a large crowd shows up anyway. He doesn't sigh and sail off. He has compassion on them and heals their sick (Matthew 14:13-14). So when your plans get interrupted, remember that Jesus can meet people in the middle of His own tired day.

Then the disciples do the math, and the math says send everybody away. It's a sensible plan, and Jesus still says, "They do not need to go away. You give them something to eat." (Matthew 14:16). They show up with five loaves and two fish, and Jesus says, "Bring them here to Me." (Matthew 14:18). He didn't ask for more first. He asked for what they had, put it in His hands, and that was enough.

So here's the big idea, baker. What you have looks small next to what's needed, and that's okay, because Jesus doesn't ask you to cover the gap. He asks you to bring Him what you've got, then He blesses it and hands it out. They all ate and were satisfied, with twelve basketfuls left over (Matthew 14:20). That's why my ovens stay ready: I bring the little bag of chocolate chips, and I let Him handle the rest!
